title: Nintendo's Long History with GTA Seems to Have Met Its End
description: According to Polygon, there is no sign of GTA 6 or GTA 5 on Switch 2. While past Rockstar titles came to Nintendo, this partnership may be shifting.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## The Shifting Relationship Between Rockstar and Nintendo

As the gaming industry looks ahead to the next generation of hardware, the strategies of major publishers continue to draw intense scrutiny. According to a recent report by Polygon, the long-standing relationship between Rockstar Games and Nintendo appears to be reaching a crossroads, particularly regarding the absence of major Grand Theft Auto titles on Nintendo's hardware.

Historically, Rockstar and Nintendo platforms have crossed paths despite the vastly different hardware profiles of Nintendo systems compared to other consoles and PC. Rockstar previously brought both *L.A. Noire* and the original *Red Dead Redemption* to Nintendo's ecosystem, proving that some of the publisher's acclaimed titles could successfully transition to portable-hybrid hardware with the right technical approach.

## The Notable Absence of GTA 5 and GTA6

However, the situation surrounding the *Grand Theft Auto* franchise paints a different picture. Currently, there is no sign of *GTA 6*, or even its predecessor *GTA 5*, making an appearance on Nintendo's successor console (often referred to as Switch 2). Industry observers note that this gap is likely driven by the massive scale, cutting-edge technical demands, and complex engine architecture of modern Rockstar flagships, especially an upcoming blockbuster like *GTA 6*.

Developing and optimizing a monumental open-world experience designed for high-end next-generation hardware presents immense technical hurdles when translated to Nintendo's hardware philosophy. Because of this, it appears that Rockstar's historical willingness to port select older titles to Nintendo systems may not extend to its most demanding contemporary flagships.

## Editor's Take

While Rockstar has occasionally supported Nintendo platforms with titles like *Red Dead Redemption* and *L.A. Noire*, the complete absence of *GTA 5* and *GTA 6* on the horizon suggests a pragmatic shift. Rockstar is likely prioritizing raw performance platforms for its heaviest hitters, meaning fans hoping for Grand Theft Auto on Nintendo hardware will likely need to look elsewhere.
